statement: The prime number theorem holds with an error smaller than every fixed negative logarithmic power. Mertens’ estimates give X p≤y 1 p = log log y + O(1), Y p≤y  1 − 1 p  ∼ e−γE log y , where γE is Euler’s constant. For fixed A, C > 0, uniformly for r ≤ (log y)C and (a, r) = 1, the Siegel–Walfisz estimate is #{p ≤ y : p ≡ a (mod r)} = Li(y) φ(r) + OA,C  y (log y)A  . Its constants need not be effective.
